item.description: Diplomats for China and the US in Latin America have traded brickbats on social media over alleged espionage risks posed by Chinese tech firms in the region, in the latest sign of the two powers’ unfolding strategic tensions in the western hemisphere. US assistant secretary of state for western hemisphere affairs Juan Pablo Segura named telecoms giants Huawei Technologies, ZTE and Hytera, surveillance equipment makers Hikvision and Dahua, and drone heavyweight DJI in a post on social media on... item.title: La generación Z ha roto un viejo estereotipo de los jóvenes: han dejado de ser "ninis" para ser "sisis"
item.description: Tras la crisis de 2012, un fenómeno creció entre los jóvenes en España. El fracaso escolar los dejaba fuera del sistema educativo tras completar la etapa de educación obligatoria y las escasas oportunidades laborales les dejaban fuera del mercado laboral: eran los "ninis" que ni estudiaban ni trabajaban. Los datos están demostrando que, en 2026, la generación Z está dibujando un panorama muy diferente con respecto a su integración al mundo laboral. Tras la pandemia, el 26% de los jóvenes de entre 16 y 29 años que trabajaba, también estudiaba. Hoy lo hace el 33% de los jóvenes en esa… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Cops used electrocution gloves to subdue high school students in Omaha, now the school district and parents are pleading with police to stop
item.description: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to acquire electric-shock gloves for $20 million. These devices were recently used on two Omaha high school students by officers. Omaha's superintendent requested the police stop using the gloves in schools. Bellevue police will continue carrying the controversial devices for student safety. Experts and parents criticize the gloves as abusive and inappropriate for schools. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: UK woman ‘saved’ by cancer trial cycles 186 miles to thank her hospital
item.description: Julie Rose pedaled an impressive 186 miles to The Royal Marsden hospital, fueled by optimism after a successful clinical trial for her rare cancer. Within six months of beginning her new medication, her tumors had shown significant reduction. This inspiring journey not only pays tribute to her medical team but also drives vital funding towards innovative cancer research for improved, personalized treatment options. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Children make up half of mpox cases in Guinea-Bissau as epidemic spreads
item.description: West African country reports 46 suspected cases in outbreak declared in July, amid fears virus may be spreading undetected More than half of the mpox cases reported in Guinea-Bissau have been among children, local authorities have said, almost two months since the country announced an epidemic. A national outbreak was declared on 4 July, just over a week after a 27-year-old woman became the first confirmed case of mpox in the west African country. Since then, there have been seven confirmed cases and 46 suspected cases. Half of those patients have been children, with 16 under the age of four… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Meet Iris Shen, the 17-year-old Texas student who tested potential blood-cancer drugs in clams and her research won $150,000
item.description: A talented teen from Texas, Iris Shen, has triumphed in a renowned science contest with her groundbreaking research. By investigating a potential cancer treatment using clams, she discovered that these creatures exhibit effects akin to human cells. Her innovative work highlights marine bivalves as a viable and ethical alternative for animal testing, directly tackling the pressing ethical and financial challenges associated with conventional methods. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
